items.title: Decoding Clickbait: The Impact of Clickbait Types and Structures on Cognitive and Emotional Responses in Online Interactions

judge.evidence_empirical: Using electroencephalography with 32 internet-experienced participants, we analyzed how these different clickbait configurations affect engagement and processing.
judge.evidence_topic: This study delves into the influence of clickbait types (hyperbole, insinuation, visual rhetoric, and puzzle) and structures (emotion-label and emotion-laden words) on user cognitive and emotional responses in an online environment.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga os efeitos de manchetes clickbait sobre respostas cognitivas e emocionais de usuários, utilizando EEG com 32 participantes, o que atende ao pedido. O estudo é empírico, o método e achado extraídos correspondem ao resumo.

items.title: Click me…! The influence of clickbait on user engagement in social media and the role of digital nudging

judge.evidence_empirical: For this, we use a data set of more than 4,400 Facebook posts from 10 different news sources to analyze how clickbait in post headlines and in post text influences user engagement.
judge.evidence_topic: We analyze the impact of clickbait on user interaction on Facebook in the form of liking, sharing and commenting.
judge.reason: O resumo descreve um estudo empírico com dados de engajamento de usuários, diretamente sobre o efeito de clickbait em interações no Facebook. O achado extraído reflete exatamente o que o resumo afirma: certas características aumentam a interação, outras diminuem. O tipo de estudo e método estão em conformidade com o resumo.

items.title: You won't believe it! Truth judgments for clickbait headlines benefit (but less so) from prior exposure

judge.evidence_empirical: In two high‐powered experiments, ... Experiment 1 ( N = 241) ... Experiment 2 ( N = 291)
judge.evidence_topic: we investigated how prior exposure to statements presented in a clickbait format increases the perceived truth of their content
judge.reason: O achado de que a exposição prévia a manchetes clickbait aumenta o julgamento de verdade, mas em menor grau do que para afirmações comuns, é sustentado pelo resumo: “prior exposure increased the proportion of ‘true’ judgments for both non‐clickbait and clickbait content, but with a reduced effect of prior exposure for statements originally presented in a clickbait format” e “exposure to clickbait headlines can increase their content's truth judgments ... although to a lesser extent than for more regular statements”.

items.title: Exaggerated and Questioning Clickbait Headlines and Their Influence on Media Learning

judge.evidence_empirical: we conducted two online experiments, each testing a 3 (headline-type: accurate, clickbait-question, clickbait-exaggerated) × 2 (exposure: headline-only, full article) factorial. In Study 1, an online sample of US adults ( N = 629) was randomly assigned to one of six news message conditions. Study 2 ( N = 1,674) was a replication study
judge.evidence_topic: To evaluate the impact of clickbait headlines on media learning and article-related beliefs, we conducted two online experiments
judge.reason: O resumo afirma exatamente que ler o artigo completo com manchete precisa resultou no maior reconhecimento e compreensão, e que a correção no artigo não basta para superar o efeito negativo da manchete clickbait, sustentando integralmente o achado extraído.

items.title: Attention Grabbing through Forward Reference: An ERP Study on Clickbait and Top News Stories

judge.evidence_empirical: conducted an EEG experiment based on N2b and P3a.
judge.evidence_topic: how clickbait headlines influence readers’ clicking behavior and attention allocation.
judge.reason: O resumo trata dos efeitos de manchetes clickbait em leitores (atenção e comportamento de clique), usando dados próprios de EEG. O método descrito (EEG) bate com o extraído. O achado principal está integralmente presente no resumo.

items.title: Here's What to Know About Clickbait: Effects of Image, Headline and Editing on Audience Attitudes

judge.evidence_empirical: This experimental study examines responses to three features of news practice
judge.evidence_topic: whether traditional or clickbait headlines are associated with better memory for story details.
judge.reason: O resumo confirma que a edição é a maior influência sobre qualidade/credibilidade e modera o efeito do estilo de manchete na memória, exatamente como no achado extraído.

items.title: Emotion Sells: Rage Bait vs. Information Bait in Clickbait News Headlines on Social Media

judge.evidence_empirical: Our findings show that digital-born media and conservative media were more likely to use rage bait, while no significant difference was observed in their use of information bait. In addition, rage bait headlines were linked to higher levels of audience engagement, while information bait was associated with lower engagement.
judge.evidence_topic: This study examined clickbait headlines on social media, focusing on which types of news organizations tend to use this content strategy and whether these strategies effectively drive audience engagement.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga os efeitos de manchetes clickbait no engajamento da audiência, enquadrando-se no tema. É empírico, com análise de dados de engajamento, e o método extraído corresponde ao resumo. O achado principal está totalmente respaldado pelo resumo.

items.title: Shocking secret you won't believe! Emotional arousal in clickbait headlines

judge.evidence_empirical: An experiment was conducted primarily to examine the levels of emotional arousal evoked by two treatment groups of online news headlines, news and clickbait, compared to a neutral control group. Emotional arousal was assessed using two approaches – pupillary dilation response recorded by an eye-tracking device and the Self-Assessment Manikin (SAM)
judge.evidence_topic: how clickbait headlines affect online users’ emotional and behavioral responses
judge.reason: O achado extraído corresponde exatamente ao que o resumo relata: manchetes clickbait geram mais excitação emocional do que as neutras, mas menos que as de notícias, e a excitação emocional prevê significativamente a intenção de ler notícias.

items.title: Effects of Clickbait Headlines on User Responses: An Empirical Investigation

judge.evidence_empirical: An experiment was conducted on two groups of news headlines—traditional news and clickbait— to provide empirical evidence of the effects of clickbait on online users.
judge.evidence_topic: This study investigates the influence of a conventional method of delivering news headlines, clickbait, on online users’ perceptions and responses.
judge.reason: O resumo afirma que o estudo investiga a influência de manchetes clickbait nas percepções e respostas de usuários online, utilizando um experimento com dois grupos e modelagem de equações estruturais. O achado principal extraído é sustentado diretamente: o resumo diz que clickbait evoca excitação e curiosidade, e que a curiosidade é o principal determinante da intenção de ler, enquanto a qualidade do conhecimento percebida é o principal fator para compartilhar.

items.title: Aggregation, Clickbait and Their Effect on Perceptions of Journalistic Credibility and Quality

judge.evidence_empirical: two online experiments to test readers’ perceptions
judge.evidence_topic: Results also suggest clickbait headlines may lower perceptions of credibility and quality.
judge.reason: The abstract states that aggregation has little effect on credibility/quality and that clickbait headlines may lower these perceptions, which matches the extracted finding precisely.

items.title: AI vs. Human-Authored Headlines: Evaluating the Effectiveness, Trust, and Linguistic Features of ChatGPT-Generated Clickbait and Informative Headlines in Digital News

judge.evidence_empirical: tested on a sample of 624 students from Timisoara, Romania, asked to evaluate the qualities of a mix of human-written vs. AI-generated headlines.
judge.evidence_topic: Clickbait headlines, regardless of their source, were considered misleading and rated as manipulative (44.7%). In addition, 54.5% of respondents reported a decrease in trust regarding publications that frequently use clickbait techniques.
judge.reason: O artigo trata de efeitos de manchetes clickbait em leitores, é empírico com dados de questionário, os dados extraídos (tipo de estudo e método) correspondem ao resumo, e o achado principal é sustentado literalmente pelo trecho citado.

items.title: Analyzing Sensationalism in News on Twitter (X): Clickbait Journalism by Legacy vs. Online-Native Outlets and the Consequences for User Engagement

judge.evidence_empirical: First, a manual content analysis of 1,440 tweets by news media organizations was conducted, identifying sensationalism through ten features. Second, an automated content analysis was conducted on a dataset of 25,600 tweets, replicating the manual coding process.
judge.evidence_topic: a positive relationship was found between the number of sensationalist features employed and the favorite count, confirming the effectiveness of clickbaits.
judge.reason: The article directly investigates the effects of clickbait (sensationalist features) on user engagement metrics (favorites and retweets), using empirical data from tweets. The abstract fully supports both the topic relevance and the extracted finding about greater sensationalism among online-native outlets and a positive link to engagement.

items.title: Clickbait-style headlines and journalism credibility in Sub-Saharan Africa: Exploring audience perceptions

judge.evidence_empirical: This experimental study
judge.evidence_topic: This experimental study, therefore, set out to understand how the audience perceives clickbait-style headlines in relations to media credibility. Particularly, the study examined whether the Zambian and Tanzanian online news consumers observe the same distinction in the credibility of news content alleged to exist between clickbait and traditional news reporting
judge.reason: O artigo investiga os efeitos das manchetes clickbait na percepção de credibilidade jornalística por consumidores de notícias online na Zâmbia e Tanzania, alinhando-se com o tema solicitado. Trata-se de um estudo empírico (experimental) com dados própios, satisfazendo o critéio empírico. O tipo de estudo e o méodo extraídos coincidem com o relato do resumo. O achado principal extraí do é plenamente amparado pelo resumo, que reporta evidências estatísticas de efeitos negativos das manchetes clickbait sobre a credibilidade jornalística percebida.

items.title: Did clickbait crack the code on virality?

judge.evidence_empirical: Using a controlled experiment, we confirm that high-emotional headlines are shared more and show evidence that clickbait often leads to inferences of maniplative intent and source derogation.
judge.evidence_topic: Although clickbait is a ubiquitous tactic in digital media, we challenge the popular belief that clickbait systematically leads to enhanced sharing of online content on social media.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga efeitos de clickbait no compartilhamento de conteúdo online, mas não especifica que se trata de leitores de notícias, conforme exigido pelo pedido. O resumo fala em 'digital media' e 'online content' sem mencionar notícias.

items.title: Seeing is not always believing: an exploratory study of clickbait in WeChat

judge.evidence_empirical: the authors collected longitudinal data in collaboration with a leading company that operates more than 500 WeChat official accounts in China. Econometric analysis was employed for empirical validation.
judge.evidence_topic: the purpose includes: 'what characteristics of clickbait headlines attract user clicks'; findings: 'hyperbole, insinuation, and visual rhetoric entice users to click the baited headlines'
judge.reason: The extracted main finding is directly supported by the abstract, which reports that hyperbole, insinuation, and visual rhetoric attract clicks and that there is an inverted U-shaped relationship between clickbait headlines and visit traffic.

items.title: The mechanism leads to successful clickbait promotion in WeChat social media platforms

judge.evidence_empirical: A total of three studies were employed online... All data were sourced randomly from 729 respondents in China.
judge.evidence_topic: This study aims to examine how the clickbait headlines influence... purchasing intention of customers on social commerce through social media platforms.
judge.reason: O artigo examina efeitos de clickbait sobre usuários (credibilidade, intenção de compra) por meio de experimentos online com 729 respondentes na China, enquadrando-se no tema e no recorte (estudo empírico com dados próprios de leitores/usuários). O tipo de estudo e método extraídos batem com o resumo. O achado principal extraído é integralmente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Semantic structure of clickbait headlines and internet user activities

judge.evidence_empirical: The material of the study is 4900 headlines of Russian news media for May 2019, provided by the news aggregator SMI2. ... having analyzed CTR values growth/decrease
judge.evidence_topic: explores the relation between clickability, measured in click-through rate (CTR) with the system of meanings the headline comprises
judge.reason: O artigo investiga a relação entre os significados de manchetes clickbait e o comportamento de cliques dos leitores (CTR), usando dados empíricos de engajamento. O método extraído, o tamanho da amostra e o achado principal são consistentes com o resumo.

items.title: The curiosity effect: Information seeking in the contemporary news environment

judge.evidence_empirical: In two studies (a lab experiment and a field test), we examine how the presentation of news information—traditional, summary news headlines or clickbait, curiosity news headlines—influences the attitudinal and behavioral components of news seeking.
judge.evidence_topic: This research investigates how digital news headlines influence contemporary news information seeking. ... examine how the presentation of news information—traditional, summary news headlines or clickbait, curiosity news headlines—influences the attitudinal and behavioral components of news seeking.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga efeitos de manchetes clickbait em leitores, com estudos empíricos próprios (experimento de laboratório e teste de campo). O tipo de estudo e método extraídos batem com o resumo. O achado principal é totalmente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: The Effect of Clickbait Headlines on Tribunnews.Com Online News Articles on the Reading Interest of Generation Z at FKI UMS

judge.evidence_empirical: This study employs a quantitative approach using a survey method through a questionnaire distributed to 113 respondents.
judge.evidence_topic: This study aims to analyze the effect of clickbait headlines on Tribunnews.com on the reading interest of Generation Z students at the Faculty of Communication and Informatics, Universitas Muhammadiyah Surakarta.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda diretamente o efeito de manchetes clickbait sobre leitores, sem recorte político, alinhando-se ao pedido. É um estudo empírico com dados próprios (questionário com 113 respondentes). Os dados extraídos refletem fielmente o tipo de estudo, método e tamanho da amostra. O achado principal está plenamente respaldado pelo trecho do resumo indicado.

items.title: Pengaruh Berita Clickbait Terhadap Kepercayaan pada Media di Era Attention Economy

judge.evidence_empirical: Data penelitian ini dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner jenis angket tertutup. Kuesioner disebar kepada 100 responden
judge.evidence_topic: Penelitian ini bertujuan mengidentifikasi apakah terdapat pengaruh berita clickbait terhadap kepercayaan pada media.
judge.reason: O resumo afirma que houve 'pengaruh sebesar 28,4 persen' e um 'pengaruh positivo', indicando que a influência do clickbait sobre a confiança é positiva e que os leitores continuam confiando, desde que a notícia siga os conceitos de confiança. O achado extraído, ao contrário, fala em 'redução de 28,4% na confiança', o que não é sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: English Clickbait Language Features Which Attract Thai Tertiary EFL Learners

judge.evidence_empirical: News headlines were presented to 18 participants to rate which news headline they would choose. Then, the rationales behind the selection were elicited using an interview.
judge.evidence_topic: This study explored how likely its Thai participants were to choose to read an article with a clickbait headline, together with how the reasons given for choosing clickbait headlines correspond to the linguistic features found in the headlines.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda diretamente os efeitos de manchetes clickbait sobre leitores, com dados de participantes tailandeses. É um estudo empírico com coleta de dados própria (18 participantes, escolha de manchetes e entrevistas). O tipo de estudo (métodos mistos) e o método descrito no dado extraído correspondem ao resumo. O achado principal está integralmente apoiado no resumo, que menciona a preferência por manchetes não‑clickbait, a relevância pessoal como fator principal e a influência de números e perguntas sem resposta nas escolhas não‑acadêmicas.
